title: Mendel's Laws of Genetics
text: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, conducted pea plant breeding experiments in the 1860s that established the fundamental principles of heredity. Mendel's Law of Segregation states that each organism carries two alleles for each trait, which segregate during gamete formation so each gamete carries only one allele. Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment states that genes for different traits assort independently of each other during gamete formation (later refined to apply to genes on different chromosomes). Mendel's work was rediscovered in 1900 and forms the basis of classical genetics. The concept of dominant and recessive alleles explains why some traits appear in offspring even when absent in parents.
